subject: SIG: Clarify breach-notification timelines & contact handoffs
messages:
From: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@greenco.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenCo Vendor Security <vendor-security@greenco.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG - breach-notification timelines (section 3)

Hi Naomi,

We're reviewing your SIG responses and have a few follow-ups specifically on the breach-notification process (SIG section 3). Two quick asks: 1) what is your committed notification window to customers after you confirm unauthorized access? 2) who are the 24/7 escalation contacts (names, roles, and sequential handoff plan) we can include in our internal playbook?

I've attached a short PDF with the related SIG questions called "SIG_section_3_questions.pdf" — I've annotated where we need a short paragraph or a roster file.

Because GreenCo operates across EMEA and NA, we also need to understand how cross-border notification timing differs if the incident impacts EU-region accounts. Please keep the answers high-level (we'll follow up for evidence).

Can you get back by EOD Wednesday PST? We're trying to close this section before our procurement review Thursday.

Thanks,
Elena Petrova
Head of Vendor Security | GreenCo
elena.petrova@greenco.com

[attachment: SIG_section_3_questions.pdf (pdf)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@greenco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG - breach notification timelines (section 3)

Hi Elena — thanks for the clarity and the annotated PDF. I'm copying Marcus (Director, Trust & Safety) and Aditya (Head of Legal Ops) to align on timelines and approvals.

Short answers up front:
- Customer notification objective: we aim to notify confirmed affected customers within 72 hours of confirmation of unauthorized access, subject to safety and legal assessment.
- 24/7 escalation / handoff: initial triage by on-call SRE -> Incident Response Lead -> Trust & Safety Director -> Legal Counsel for notification sign-off. I'll attach an excerpt from our IR playbook (redwood_ir_playbook_excerpt.pdf) and a sanitized on-call roster for the SIG (redwood_ir_oncall_roster.csv).

A few clarifying notes:
- "Confirmation" means technical verification that an access control boundary was breached and customer-affecting data exposure is plausible. We don't start the 72-hour clock on detection alone if we need a short technical validation window (typically 4-8 hours).
- For EU accounts, we coordinate immediate notification to our DPO and Legal (within the same 72-hour objective where feasible), but cross-border regulatory notification (e.g., to supervisory authorities) follows local law — we will provide customers the timeline we communicated to regulators if applicable.

Marcus/Aditya — can you confirm any legal constraints we should call out for GreenCo (e.g., regulator-specific windows that could shorten the customer notice window)? Also please confirm if the on-call roster file is okay to share as-is for the SIG.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Security & Privacy Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

[attachments: redwood_ir_playbook_excerpt.pdf, redwood_ir_oncall_roster.csv]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@greenco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG - breach notification timelines (section 3)

Hi all — quick confirmation from Trust & Safety / Legal Ops side.

1) The 72-hour customer notification objective Naomi outlined is our standard operational target and is consistent with our SOC 2 incident handling commitments. We will escalate any potential regulator-triggering incidents immediately to Legal.

2) For EU-regulated data, we treat supervisor-notification obligations as separate from customer notification. Practically: if a regulatory filing is required (per DPAs), that may impose additional timelines or reporting content; we'll include a line in the SIG response explaining that regulator timelines can override customer-friendly notification cadence.

3) On-call roster: Naomi, the CSV is fine for the SIG (sanitized names + roles). For contract-level sharing (e.g., in a marketplace listing) we'll redact direct phone lines.

Action items: Marcus to send a one-paragraph legal caveat for the SIG; Naomi to produce the final two short paragraphs for SIG section 3 (one on timeline, one on contacts/hand-off). Aditya to review for any contractual exposures.

Marcus Lin
Director, Trust & Safety | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
